_comment: Multicam screencast: a screen recording that captured NO audio, plus the iPhone take that carries the narration. camera_rotate is 'none' on purpose -- IMG_2695 has a rotation=-90 display matrix that is WRONG (the phone was mounted flat and iOS guessed), and honouring it lays the shot on its side. Check a frame before trusting that tag either way.

film._why: He turns away at 7:37 of the finished film and delivers the last sentence in profile, to a phone that is switched off. The last line he gives to camera is the meta sign-off about how the film was shot, so the film ends on that. end_pad restores the 0.8s of air the transcript default would have given, which a phrase-resolved bound does not.

anchors._why: the Resume-session picker opens on screen at 101.1-102.3 and he says 'here are several sessions' over it
he selects the 'Skills wrapping these:' line at 442.3-442.5 while saying 'several skills'

cut._comment: force_over: a silence this long goes even if the screen is moving. camera_when_frozen_over: once the screen has sat still longer than this, show the camera full-frame instead -- a PiP does not rescue a dead frame. 100 catches the 167s stretch here; 60 would also catch the 92s of empty prompt at the start, which is a bigger editorial change.

bookends._comment: PXL_...160930856 was recorded after the fact specifically to open the film -- he says so in it: 'на початку відео я ставлю цей фрагмент'. PXL_...155547234 is the setup take and is SILENT (0 words transcribed), so it can only work as picture under someone else's sound. It cuts in exactly where the intro says the film combines files from different phones, and shows the two-phone rig.

name_labels._why: The opening bookend runs full-frame camera from 0 to ~8.2s of film time, where the b-roll of the two-phone rig cuts in. The card fades up once he is talking and is gone before that cut, so it never sits over footage it does not belong to.
name_labels.name: Oleksandr Gamaniuk
name_labels.title: CEO, Instafill.ai

image_overlays._why: End card. `at` is negative on purpose -- it means 'this many seconds before the end', so re-cutting the film (a different min_silence, another bookend) moves the card with it instead of stranding it at a timecode that no longer exists. The film's last line is the meta sign-off about how it was shot, so the card lands over that and holds to black. The treatment is what stops the card fighting the footage: he is still talking under it, and B&W + blur + dim puts him behind the type without freezing or cutting him off.
